stem: A client with a hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula is reviewing home access care. Which statement shows correct understanding?

options.A: I will check the access every day for redness or warmth and make sure I can still feel the usual vibration.
options.B: I only need to check the access on days when I receive dialysis.
options.C: If I cannot feel the usual vibration after dialysis, I can wait until the next scheduled treatment to report it.
options.D: Redness and warmth over the access are expected unless I also develop a fever.

rationale: NIDDK instructs clients to protect the hemodialysis access, wash the area daily, check for warmth or redness, and confirm the vibration produced by blood flow; the dialysis center should be notified if the vibration cannot be felt. A reflects correct surveillance. B omits daily monitoring, C delays reporting possible loss of flow, and D incorrectly normalizes local infection findings.
educational_objective: Teach daily AV-fistula surveillance for infection findings and the expected blood-flow vibration, with prompt reporting if the vibration is lost.
source_organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), NIH
source_locator: Take care of your access: wash area daily; check warmth/redness; a working access has a palpable vibration; notify the dialysis center if the vibration cannot be felt. Possible problems: access infection or poor blood flow/blockage.
source_claim_supported: Daily AV-access care includes checking for infection and the expected blood-flow vibration and reporting loss of that vibration.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Printed page 14, Physiological Adaptation: manage care of a client receiving hemodialysis; recognize client complications and intervene.
correction_summary: Replaced redundant thrill/bruit recall with actionable client teaching and corrected the blueprint from Basic Care and Comfort to Physiological Adaptation.
audit_findings: NIDDK directly supports every correct teaching element and contradicts B-D. This avoids duplicating Q1306 by testing client self-care rather than thrombosis recognition. No unsupported numeric/device rule remains. Blueprint matches NCSBN 2026 hemodialysis management. Independent adversarial second pass found no second answer, cueing or ambiguity.

final_reaudit_scope: NIDDK AV-access care; NCSBN 2026 hemodialysis management; A-D/adversarial review
